paper.title: PhysMem: Scaling Test-Time Memory for Embodied Physical Reasoning
paper.central_claim: A scientific memory loop lets frozen VLM robot planners learn task-specific physical principles at test time; targeted verification before application makes retained rules more useful than direct retrieval and supports changed-condition deployment.

Additional admission criterion in Appendix A-D; main-text acceptance description is not exhaustive.

evidence.quote: MemER [ 55 ] and MemoryVLA [ 51 ] require parameter updates (imitation finetuning or end-to-end VLA training); running their full systems would take us out of the frozen-base setting, so we benchmark training-free proxies that isolate their retrieval mechanism

Baseline rates and unequal token consumption; full rates are on same table line.

signatures.object: Frozen VLM planner context and episodic/hypothesis/principle stores, compared with empty or raw-retrieval memory
signatures.information: RGB, options, outcome feedback and symbolic task state; simulator includes blockers and dependency features; physical references and strategic prompt details are elided. No parameter updates.
signatures.operation: Cluster symbolic experiences, draft typed Avoid/Prefer/Sequence hypotheses, update action-conditioned confidence, promote/refute and fold supporting episodes. Retrieve five relevant principles and active hypotheses.
signatures.output: Persistent natural-language principles plus confidence and expiring source memory
signatures.conditions: Repeat tasks with outcomes, symbolic clustering and sufficiently capable planner; targeted-interaction scheduling is underspecified.
signatures.feedback: Action success, failure and contradiction/resonance, rather than final episode success alone
signatures.selection_rule: Promote confidence >=0.8, >=3 supporting episodes, >=85% support accuracy; refute <=0.3 and >=2 contradictions
signatures.selection_data: Experiences acquired during deployment; construction episodes are not independent test episodes
signatures.persistence: Episodic capacity 3000; promotion folds experiences; long-term principles decay at 0.995; memory snapshots saved during 500 episodes
signatures.later_use: Principles injected into later episodes and frozen snapshot tests of 50 held-out episodes; ID-acquired prior also tested on OOD variants
signatures.claimed_effect: Medium insertion 76% vs no memory53%, raw retrieval23%, reflection61%; OOD advantages differ with dynamics
signatures.failure_boundary: Over-generalization, 2-4 episode correction lag, ignored principles; prompts and privileged blocker channel limit attribution

gap.author_gap: Frozen VLMs have declarative physics but lack task-specific contact knowledge; stale unverified replay can hurt when objects or physics change.
gap.checked_gap: Fixed-executor results and raw-retrieval failures substantiate a recurrent-task memory problem. They do not establish discovery of new physics or dominance over trained memory systems.

claims.setting: OOD grid configurations, balls and stone combinations; same xArm6

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Authors report fixed-planner insertion gains and retained memory snapshot performance on held-out episodes, plus prior-only 8/10 success on unseen stone combinations. Broad physical-understanding and verification-before-any-application interpretations are not established. Narrow transfer label comes from frozen ID prior on explicitly unseen configurations, not adaptive OOD data or real-hardware presence alone.
